subject: English
topic: Cloze test / fill-blank II — mixed tiers

questions.stem: Read the passage and choose the option that correctly fills both blanks. A good teacher does not merely _____(i)_____ information to students but also _____(ii)_____ a genuine love for learning in them. Education, at its core, is not simply about clearing examinations; it is about shaping curious and responsible individuals. The most vibrant classrooms are those where questions are welcomed and imagination is celebrated. A teacher who truly inspires can transform a student's entire outlook on life. Which option correctly fills blanks (i) and (ii)?
questions.explanation: A is correct. 'Impart information' is a standard collocation meaning to convey or pass on knowledge — teachers impart wisdom, not transfer or discard it. 'Kindles a love' means to ignite or spark enthusiasm; 'kindle' specifically collocates with emotions, passions, and interests (kindle curiosity, kindle affection). Option C fails because 'impose information' is an invalid phrase — you impose rules or penalties, not information. Option B's 'suppresses a love for learning' directly contradicts the positive, inspiring tone of the passage. Grammar note: 'instil' (Option D) is correct for blank (ii) but 'discard information' makes no sense in context.

questions.stem: Select the pair of words that best fills the blanks in the passage. Regular physical exercise greatly _____(i)_____ the body's immune defences and enables a person to _____(ii)_____ common infections far more effectively. A sedentary lifestyle, in contrast, increases vulnerability to chronic diseases and persistent fatigue. Even a brisk thirty-minute walk each day can bring significant and lasting health benefits. Medical experts now emphasise that movement is as vital to well-being as a balanced and nutritious diet. Which pair correctly fills blanks (i) and (ii)?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Fortifies' collocates precisely with 'immune defences' — to fortify means to strengthen defensively, exactly what exercise achieves. 'Withstand infections' means to endure or successfully resist them, a natural collocation in medical writing. Option C: 'boosts' could loosely fit blank (i), but 'succumb to infections' means to yield to them — the exact opposite of what exercise enables. Option D: 'strains the immune defences' implies putting damaging stress on them, which describes the effect of illness rather than exercise. Option A: 'weakens' is the direct opposite of the passage's central argument. Collocation note: 'fortify' always implies defensive strengthening — fortify walls, fortify resolve, fortify the immune system.

questions.stem: Choose the option that best fills both blanks in the passage. A democracy can only _____(i)_____ when its citizens actively and meaningfully participate in the electoral process. Those who choose not to vote inadvertently _____(ii)_____ their political power to individuals who may not reflect the majority's wishes at all. Civil society organisations, the media, and educational institutions share the responsibility of encouraging voter participation. An informed and engaged electorate is the true foundation of a healthy republic. Which option correctly fills blanks (i) and (ii)?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Flourish' means to grow and thrive under ideal conditions — a democracy flourishes when citizens participate fully. 'Cede' is the precise political and legal term for formally yielding power or rights to another party; voters who abstain cede their political voice. Option D: 'thrive' is close in meaning to 'flourish' for blank (i), but 'acquire power' directly contradicts the sentence — the meaning is that power passes to others when citizens don't vote, not that non-voters gain power. Option C: 'decline' is the opposite of what a democracy does under active participation. Option A: 'reclaim' means to take something back, which reverses the direction of the sentence. Vocab note: 'cede' (yield formally) vs 'concede' (acknowledge defeat) — common exam confusion.

questions.stem: Read the passage and select the option that correctly fills all three blanks. A well-written novel has the power to _____(i)_____ the reader into a world entirely different from their own, one shaped by the author's imagination and empathy. Great writers do not merely _____(ii)_____ stories; they hold a mirror to society and compel us to examine our deepest values. Books that have _____(iii)_____ the test of time continue to move and provoke readers long after their authors are gone. Literature, at its finest, is a conversation that effortlessly spans centuries. Which option correctly fills blanks (i), (ii), and (iii)?
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Transport the reader' is a fixed literary collocation meaning to carry someone imaginatively to another world — 'withdraw' (to pull back) and 'carry' (too literal and mechanical) do not capture this sense. 'Narrate stories' is the precise literary verb, more formal and apt than 'tell' in this elevated register. 'Withstood the test of time' is a set idiom meaning to endure long-term judgment — this is a fixed phrase and the only natural collocate. Option B: 'failed the test of time' is the direct opposite of the intended meaning. Option D: 'defy the test of time' is non-standard; you withstand or stand the test, not defy it. Option A: 'fabricate stories' implies deliberate deception, an uncharitable framing for literary authors. Grammar rule: 'withstand' takes a direct object without a preposition — 'withstand the test', not 'withstand against the test'.

questions.stem: Read the passage carefully and choose the word pair that correctly fills the blanks. India's river systems have been _____(i)_____ to the survival and growth of civilisations for thousands of years, nurturing agriculture, trade, and culture along their fertile banks. Today, however, many of these rivers are under serious threat due to industrial pollution, rampant encroachment, and indiscriminate disposal of waste. If urgent steps are not taken, the rivers that have _____(ii)_____ life for countless generations will become irreversible ecological disasters. River conservation must therefore become a national priority, not merely a seasonal campaign. Which option correctly fills blanks (i) and (ii)?
questions.explanation: D is correct. 'Central to the survival and growth of civilisations' — rivers were the very nucleus of early human settlements (Indus, Ganges, Yamuna); 'central' expresses core-position status better than 'crucial', which merely means important. 'Sustained life' = kept life going continuously over generations — a precise ecological collocation (you sustain life, you do not terminate or disrupt it). Option C: 'crucial' is plausible for blank (i) but 'terminated life' is a stark contradiction — rivers nurtured life, not ended it. Option B: 'disrupted life' implies harm, the direct opposite of what healthy rivers historically provide. Option A: 'marginal' means peripheral or minor, directly opposite to rivers' foundational civilisational role. Collocation note: 'sustain life' is a fixed phrase in biology and ecology meaning to keep alive indefinitely — contrast with 'maintain life' (keep going) and 'support life' (provide conditions for).

questions.stem: Read the following passage and select the option that correctly fills all three blanks. India's trade policy has _____(i)_____ considerably over the past three decades, shifting from a largely protectionist stance towards greater _____(ii)_____ with global markets. This transformation has not been without its contradictions — while export-oriented industries have flourished, domestic producers in several sectors have been forced to _____(iii)_____ intense foreign competition that threatens their livelihoods. Designing frameworks that promote growth without marginalising vulnerable domestic sectors remains the central challenge for policymakers today. Which option correctly fills blanks (i), (ii), and (iii)?
questions.explanation: B is correct. 'Evolved' captures gradual, substantive change over time — India's post-1991 liberalisation is precisely described as economic evolution, not stagnation or regression. 'Integration with global markets' is the standard economic term for deepened connectedness with international trade (seen in WTO commitments, FTAs). 'Contend with competition' is a fixed phrase meaning to actively face and manage competitive pressure. Option A: 'stagnated' means declined or remained unchanged — the opposite of liberalisation. Option C: 'isolation' directly contradicts 'shifting towards greater... with global markets', making blank (ii) self-defeating within the sentence. Option D: 'regressed' implies moving backward, contradicting the forward liberalisation trajectory; 'ignore competition' is economically incoherent — domestic producers cannot simply disregard foreign rivals without consequence. Vocab note: 'contend with' (cope with adversity) vs 'contend for' (compete to win) — different prepositions, different meanings.

questions.stem: Select the option that correctly fills all three blanks in the passage. The scientific community has long grappled with communicating complex research to a general audience in ways that neither _____(i)_____ the facts nor _____(ii)_____ the public's genuine capacity to understand them. Effective science communication requires a careful balance — simplifying without distorting and engaging without _____(iii)_____ to sensationalism. This balance, when consistently achieved, builds lasting public trust in scientific institutions and the knowledge they produce. Which option correctly fills blanks (i), (ii), and (iii)?
questions.explanation: C is correct. 'Distort the facts' = to misrepresent or warp them — the sentence establishes that good science communication avoids this. 'Underestimate the public's capacity' = to think the audience is less capable than they are — the most common failure mode in science writing, hence the thing to avoid. 'Resorting to sensationalism' is a fixed idiomatic phrase; one resorts to something as a fallback — you cannot 'yield to' a method in this construction. Option A: 'clarify the facts' is inherently positive — saying communication must not clarify facts is self-defeating. Option B: 'overestimate the public's capacity' (thinking too highly of the audience) is far less common than underestimation; additionally, 'without avoiding sensationalism' would mean that using sensationalism is acceptable, which contradicts the passage's argument. Option D: 'verify the facts' is a positive journalistic duty — avoiding verification would be irresponsible, not a communication failure. Collocation note: 'resort to' is always followed by a noun or gerund and expresses a fallback choice made under pressure — it cannot be replaced by 'yield to' here without altering the preposition structure.
